summary.why: This party says that argues that Aotearoa's tax system is highly unequal, given that wages are taxed more than income from wealth. Lower-earning people have less disposable income; this party seeks to reduce how much this group is taxed.

statement: Establish an independent Te Tiriti Commission

summary.why: This party says that says that te Triti is the constitutional foundation of Aotearoa, but how te Tiriti is treated depends on the government of the day. Therefore, a crown watchdog regarding the implementation of te Tiriti is required.

statement: Convene a Māori constitutional convention as laid out in Matike Mai

summary.why: This party says that Māori constitutional sovereignty comes from He Whakaputanga o te Rangatiratanga o Nu Tireni (the 1835 declaration of independence). However, with no written constitution, Māori authority is not constitutionally enshrined as it should be. The Mātike Mai project, which was founded in 2010 to strengthen the independence of iwi and hapū, is underfunded to resource such a transition.
summary.how: This party would convene a Māori constitutional convention which will start dialogue with tangata Tiriti and both local and central government regarding New Zealand's constitutional future. It would set 2040 as a target date for constitutional change in New Zealand, and estimates that this policy would cost $220m. This would follow the recommendations of the Matike Mai report.

sources.title: A Kiwi Tax Plan — Te Pāti Māori Policy Manifesto 2026: Tax (PDF)
Pūtea Back In Your Pocket: TPM Unveils A Kiwi Tax Plan For Everyone (Press release, 2026-08-26)

statement: Invest $1 billion in Inland Revenue, the SFO, the FMA and the Financial Intelligence Unit to fight tax evasion

summary.why: The party says aggressive tax avoidance must be eliminated so everyone pays their fair share.
summary.how: This party would increase investment by $1 billion across IRD, the Serious Fraud Office, the Financial Markets Authority and the NZ Financial Intelligence Unit.

sources.title: A Kiwi Tax Plan — Te Pāti Māori Policy Manifesto 2026: Tax (PDF)

statement: Establish a $220 million Mātike Mai Fund and set 2040 as the target for constitutional transformation

summary.why: The party says Māori-led constitutional work (Mātike Mai Aotearoa) has been done but lacks resources and enforceable accountability.
summary.how: This party would fund a $220 million Mātike Mai Fund over four years to independently resource iwi, hapū and Māori to lead constitutional transformation, with 2040 as the target. It says it will not itself determine the constitutional destination.

sources.title: Te Tiriti Entrenchment Policy 2026 (PDF)
Te Pāti Māori Launches Te Tiriti Entrenchment Policy (Press release, 2026-09-01)

statement: Require a Te Tiriti Impact Statement for every Bill

summary.why: The party says governments can ignore the Waitangi Tribunal and weaken Te Tiriti protections.
summary.how: This party would require every Bill before Parliament to include a Te Tiriti Impact Statement.

sources.title: Te Pati Maori Will Make The Waitangi Tribunal Recommendations Binding (Press release, 2026-08-06)

statement: Entrench the Māori electorates in the constitution

summary.why: The party says the Māori seats are guaranteed under Te Tiriti and should not be removable by referendum (responding to NZ First's referendum proposal).
summary.how: The party says that when it forms the next government it will 'entrench the Māori seats in the constitution beyond the reach of referendums'.

sources.title: Māori Seats Are Constitutional, Not Conditional (Press release, 2026-02-13)

statement: $100 million Community Kai Fund and $100 million for regenerative Māori agriculture (Mātai Ahuwhenua)

summary.why: The party says whānau should be able to grow their own kai rather than depend on food parcels and the supermarket duopoly.
summary.how: This party would set up a $100 million Community Kai Fund for home gardens, marae māra kai and community food farms, invest an extra $100 million in Mātai Ahuwhenua for regenerative and diversified Māori land-based production, and protect Māori seed, mātauranga and Indigenous plant whakapapa including through WAI 262 protections.

sources.title: Kai Sovereignty Policy 2026 (PDF)
Te Pāti Māori Launches Kai Sovereignty Policy (Press release, 2026-09-21)

statement: Give the Commerce Commission and Electricity Authority stronger powers over power prices and profits

summary.why: The party says energy is essential infrastructure that must serve people before profit.
summary.how: This party would strengthen regulators' powers to investigate excessive pricing and profits, with structural intervention, pricing tools and enforceable remedies if regulation fails, and remove barriers to whānau and communities generating and trading energy. It sets 2035 as the target for 'Energy Sovereignty'.

sources.title: Energy Sovereignty Policy 2026 (PDF)
We Want Cheaper Power And We Want Our People To Own It (Press release, 2026-09-16)

statement: Te Kōhanga Reo Act, secure baseline funding and 20 new kōhanga reo

summary.why: The party says kōhanga reo are the heartbeat of te reo Māori revitalisation and need long-term certainty.
summary.how: This party would pass a Te Kōhanga Reo Act, lock in annual baseline funding, create a $20 million-a-year capital fund, invest $50 million to clear the backlog of around 80 kōhanga needing new builds or refurbishment, and fund 20 new kōhanga reo over three years.

sources.title: Te Pāti Māori Backs Kōhanga Reo And Kura With Long-Term Investment (Press release, 2026-10-06)

statement: $1.25 billion for kura Māori property and restore Te Ahu o Te Reo Māori

summary.why: The party says kura need fit-for-purpose buildings and the education workforce needs te reo capability.
summary.how: This party would commit $1.25 billion over five years ($250 million a year) through a ring-fenced kura Māori property plan, and restore Te Ahu o Te Reo Māori with $30 million a year.

sources.title: Te Pāti Māori Backs Kōhanga Reo And Kura With Long-Term Investment (Press release, 2026-10-06)

statement: Expand school lunches, free public transport for students, free school counselling, te reo Māori core to Year 10

summary.why: The party says Māori learners thrive when whānau are central and identity is upheld.
summary.how: Alongside the Māori Education Authority, the party's education policy includes expanding school lunches, free public transport for all students, free school counselling, making te reo Māori a core curriculum subject through Year 10, more student support and a stronger education workforce.

sources.title: Te Pāti Māori Announces Māori Education Authority To Restore Māori Success In Education (Press release, 2026-08-02)

statement: Independent Toi Māori Authority and an income programme for 1,000 Māori artists

summary.why: The party says colonisation targeted Māori artists and knowledge-holders and decisions on Toi Māori should be in Māori hands.
summary.how: This party would create a Toi Māori Authority independent of Creative New Zealand, funded at parity with it and governed by tohunga toi, and a rotating programme paying 1,000 artists at a time for 30 hours a week over two years.

sources.title: Te Pāti Māori Announces Toi Māori Authority And Artist Income Programme (Press release, 2026-10-12)

statement: $200 million over three years and an independent Takatāpui-governed Commission

summary.why: The party says decisions about takatāpui have been made without takatāpui.
summary.how: This party would commit $200 million over three years (reported as reprioritised from health, social development, housing and Māori development) and create an independent Takatāpui-governed Commission with authority over ring-fenced funding for gender-affirming kaupapa Māori healthcare, mental health and suicide prevention, safe housing, protection from violence and hate, culture and education.

sources.title: Te Pāti Māori Launches Mana Takatāpui Policy (Press release, 2026-09-23)
NZ Herald: Te Pāti Māori announces $200m fund to create Takatāpui commission

statement: Create an independent Māori Justice Authority funded from half of the Corrections, Police and Courts budgets

summary.why: The party says the justice system was imposed on Māori, breaches Te Tiriti and over-incarcerates Māori.
summary.how: This party would establish a tikanga-led Independent Māori Justice Authority with real decision-making power, funded by reallocating 50% of Vote Corrections, 50% of Vote Police and 50% of Vote Courts, and invest in kaupapa Māori legal aid and community law services.

sources.title: Justice — Te Pāti Māori Policy Manifesto 2026 (PDF)

statement: Repeal three strikes, gang and bail laws; raise the age of criminal responsibility to 16

summary.why: The party says these laws discriminate against Māori and criminalise rangatahi early.
summary.how: This party would repeal three-strikes legislation, gangs legislation, the Sentencing (Reform) Amendment Act and the Bail Amendment Act, raise the age of criminal responsibility from 10 to 16, extend the Clean Slate Act to custodial sentences, require police body cameras, replace the IPCA with a Māori-grounded oversight body and reinstate funding for cultural (s27) reports.

sources.title: Justice — Te Pāti Māori Policy Manifesto 2026 (PDF)

statement: Decriminalise drug use and close military-style bootcamps and youth justice residences

summary.why: The party says drug use is a health issue and youth residences harm rangatahi.
summary.how: This party would overhaul the Misuse of Drugs Act to treat drug use as a health issue and wipe convictions for use and possession, close military-style bootcamps immediately and youth justice residences by 2030, end solitary confinement as punishment, and (under 'electoral justice') restore voting rights for all people in Corrections facilities and lower the voting age to 16.

sources.title: Justice — Te Pāti Māori Policy Manifesto 2026 (PDF)

statement: Universal rent control and an end to no-cause evictions

summary.why: The party says renters need security amid a housing crisis.
summary.how: The party's housing policy includes supporting renters through universal rent control and repealing no-cause evictions, and taxing property investors.

sources.title: Oriini Kaipara: Prime Minister’s ‘Progress’ Ignores Housing Crisis Facing Māori And Rangatahi (Press release, 2026-01-29)

statement: Build 2,000 papakāinga homes and allocate half of new social housing to whānau Māori

summary.why: The party says Māori make up half of the social housing waitlist and homelessness is a Te Tiriti breach.
summary.how: The party's housing policy includes building 2,000 houses on papakāinga, radically increasing public housing investment, and allocating 50% of new social housing builds to whānau Māori; its Tāmaki Makaurau MP has a member's bill to prevent youth homelessness.

sources.title: Oriini Kaipara: Prime Minister’s ‘Progress’ Ignores Housing Crisis Facing Māori And Rangatahi (Press release, 2026-01-29)
Te Pāti Māori Rejects Move-on Orders: “We Will Not Police Our Way Out Of Homelessness" (Press release, 2026-02-22)

statement: Stop all sales of freehold land to offshore foreign interests

summary.why: The party says land should not be sold to overseas buyers.
summary.how: The party's housing policy includes stopping all sales of freehold land to offshore foreign interests.

sources.title: Oriini Kaipara: Prime Minister’s ‘Progress’ Ignores Housing Crisis Facing Māori And Rangatahi (Press release, 2026-01-29)

statement: Fund a Marae Resilience Package so marae can act as civil-defence hubs

summary.why: The party says marae act as frontline shelters in emergencies without formal support or funding.
summary.how: The party has called for formal recognition of marae as emergency response hubs, upfront funding for emergency supplies and infrastructure, generators, water storage and communications, and long-term investment.

sources.title: Must Fund Marae Resilience Package Ahead Of Cyclone Vaianu (Press release, 2026-04-09)

note: Made as a call on the current government (April 2026) rather than as a manifesto document.

statement: Freeze MPs' pay rises and suspend fuel excise tax (cost-of-living calls)

summary.why: The party says politicians should not get pay rises while whānau struggle, and fuel excise adds about $35 to a 50-litre fill.
summary.how: The party has called for an immediate freeze on pay rises for MPs, Ministers and the Prime Minister (with a deeper cut for Ministers and the PM), and for the immediate suspension of fuel excise tax.
